podcast.title: The "Amen Break" (1969)
podcast.body: Gregory Coleman, the drummer for The Winstons, played the seven-second drum bit in their 1969 song "Amen Brother," which became famously known as the "Amen Break." This specific drum segment is recognized as the "most sampled piece of music in the universe," appearing in nearly 6,200 songs. "It features a seven-second drum bit by Gregory Coleman. This is the most sampled piece of music in the universe."

srcs.episode: Music vs Technology Over The Years

podcast.title: Lack of Compensation and Death (Died 2006)
podcast.body: Despite his drum bit, the "Amen Break," being the "most sampled piece of music in the universe," Gregory Coleman never received any compensation for its widespread use. He tragically died homeless and destitute in 2006, highlighting a significant issue regarding artist royalties and sampling in the music industry. "According to the website, whosample.com, that bit has been used in nearly 6,200 songs, and drummer Gregory Coleman never received a penny. He died homeless and destitute in 2006."

xref.title: Lack of Royalties for Amen Break
xref.body: Despite the Amen Break from "Amen Brother" being sampled in over 5,309 songs and becoming a major part of numerous hits across hip-hop, electronic, and EDM, neither Gregory Coleman nor The Winston's received any royalties. Gregory Coleman died homeless and broke in 2006, unaware of his profound impact on music, and band leader Richard Spencer died in 2020. "Not as the case with so many samples, neither Coleman nor the Winston's have seen any royalties from this, despite the fact that this piece of music has become part of so many other songs, some of which, many of which have become major hits."
